name: Avoiding the Most Common Mistakes in DIY Bathroom Wall Tiling

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Tackling a bathroom wall tile project yourself can be really rewarding, but there are definitely some pitfalls to watch out for. A lot of folks jump in without realizing how crucial certain steps are, and that's where things can go sideways fast. Let's talk about how to avoid those common blunders so your project turns out beautifully.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: First off, don't skip the surface prep. Seriously, this is a big one! If your wall isn't clean, dry, and flat, your tiles won't lay right. You can't just tile over existing paint or damaged drywall and expect good results. Take the time to get the surface smooth and sound, repairing any holes or imperfections. Next, choosing the wrong adhesive is a common slip-up. Not all thinsets are created equal, and you need one that's compatible with your specific wall substrate and tile type. Using the wrong one can lead to tiles popping off later. Another mistake is forgetting a proper layout plan. Don't just start tiling from a random corner! Plan your layout with a reference line or ledger board to ensure you don't end up with tiny, awkward cuts at the edges or uneven rows. Lastly, consistency is key when applying thinset and setting tiles. Make sure you're using spacers and constantly checking for level and plumb to avoid lippage – that's when one tile edge sits higher than its neighbor.
